title: The Hidden Cost of WordPress: What You're Really Paying
excerpt: WordPress is free, technically. But when you add up hosting, plugins, themes, security, and developer time, most small business sites cost €1,500-€5,000 a year to run.

blocks.text: WordPress is free. You've probably heard that a dozen times. And it's technically true: the software itself costs nothing to download.

But "free" is doing a lot of heavy lifting there. When you add up what running a real WordPress site actually costs, hosting, plugins, themes, [security](/blog/wordpress-security-2026), [maintenance](/blog/website-maintenance-costs), developer time, the number gets uncomfortable fast.
Here is the breakdown.

And that's assuming nothing goes wrong.
The Costs That Don't Show Up on Invoices
1. Your time

WordPress updates can sometimes cause unexpected issues. Core updates, theme updates, plugin updates: they can conflict. You might spend an hour debugging why your contact form broke after a security patch.
If your time is worth €50/hr, two hours a month is €1,200/year. Gone.
2. Slow site = lost revenue
A slow site loses visitors and conversions. If your site makes you €2,000/month and a speed improvement increases conversions 15%, that's €300/month, €3,600/year, sitting on the table.
3. Developer lock-in
WordPress customization requires WordPress-specific knowledge. The custom theme your developer built 3 years ago? Only they can maintain it efficiently.
4. Hack recovery

WordPress powers [40%](https://w3techs.com/technologies/details/cm-wordpress) of the internet. That makes it the biggest target for automated attacks. If your site gets compromised, recovery costs €200-€2,000+ depending on severity. The risk is higher without proactive security measures.

The Real Question
Ask how much WordPress costs in maintenance, missed leads, rebuild work, and risks you do not notice.

The plugin subscriptions are visible. The developer invoices are visible. The hours debugging updates, the slow site losing customers, the operational risk of running plugin updates on a production site without a staging mirror: those are the invisible costs that compound quietly.
